clue.text: Doyle's professor might be satisfied with a second helping?

definitions.meaning: Professor ... is the hot-tempered scientist of Arthur Conan Doyle's The Lost World

definitions.text: might be satisfied with a second helping?
definitions.meaning: in a duel the one who issues the call to fight demands satisfaction and is assisted by a second

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Conan Doyle character would be happy with another plateful at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second helping' looks like more food; in duelling a second is the assistant who helps the man who demanded satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: Conan Doyle's irascible scientist, and the duellist who issued the call and is attended by a second.

clue.text: Husky as four-legged transport, say

indicators.note: say means the word is to be pronounced, giving a word with a different spelling

parts.note: a horse carries riders on four legs

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a sled dog counts as animal transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog, which fits the transport story, but it means a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, the same as a hoarse one.

clue.text: Libertine reluctant to have a port?

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A rake who is unwilling to take a drink of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink a libertine might refuse; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, from a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, and so a libertine.

clue.text: Your £1,000 one's very greatly in need of repair

indicators.note: something that needs mending is broken, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: the pound sign is L, for libra, and a thousand is M in Roman numerals
the word one with its s, all used as letters

explanation.surface: Your thousand-pound possession badly wants fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormously means to a huge degree, hugely.

clue.text: Go against North Sea conversion of this cooker

indicators.note: converting changes the form, so the letters that come before are rearranged

parts.note: v, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Refuse to have this stove adapted for natural gas from the North Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1960s and 70s British appliances were converted from town gas to North Sea natural gas, which the surface recalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas oven is a cooker fuelled by gas, the kind converted when North Sea supplies arrived.

clue.text: Main danger familiar to yachtsmen ?

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a hazard there is rocks just below the water; sailors also know the word for shortening sail

explanation.surface: A principal hazard every sailor knows about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief but is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the surface, a hazard to shipping, and also a section of sail taken in.

clue.text: Outlawry said to be foreign -it upset robbers

parts.note: a ban is a sentence of outlawry, a proscription
dit is the French for said

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the little word it upside down so it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: A remark that outlawing is foreign, and that it upset some robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian plural for brigands, a gang of outlaws or robbers.

clue.text: Rising doctor in charge to cut open snake

indicators.note: in places the reversed doctor inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the short word for doctor is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil

explanation.surface: An ambitious doctor in charge has to dissect a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the doctor upwards, as this is a down clue; 'in' is the container signal, though 'in charge' poses as one phrase meaning responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: The fer-de-lance is a venomous pit viper of tropical America, a snake named for its lance-shaped head.

clue.text: Note condition of property

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A remark about the condition a property is in.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is landed property, a large holding of land and buildings.

clue.text: Critical of officer taking notes of hand

parts.note: Capt is the abbreviation for captain, an army officer
a note of hand is a promissory note, an IOU, so several of them are IOUs

explanation.surface: Disapproving of an officer who accepts promissory notes from people.
explanation.definitionFit: A captious person is fault-finding, quick to raise trivial objections.

clue.text: Test side finished appearing displeased

parts.note: in cricket, played in Test matches, the off side is one half of the field
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A national Test cricket team is annoyed at having been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test side' reads as a national cricket team, but it is the OFF side of the cricket field; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone offended has taken umbrage and is displeased.

clue.text: Good-looking prophet?

parts.note: read not as a handsome visionary but as one who looks well, someone who sees into the future

explanation.surface: An attractive soothsayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a person who sees the future, a prophet, so a good looker in the literal sense.

clue.text: Five editors he replaced before Lent

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun, the period that comes before Lent

indicators.note: replaced means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five editors were sacked and replaced by him just before Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrovetide is the few days immediately preceding Ash Wednesday, when the Lenten fast begins.

clue.text: £22 Eve collected for a decorative housing feature

annotationWithheld.why: '£22 Eve collected for a decorative housing feature' (scan agrees) cannot give OVERMANTEL: '£22 Eve' supplies no recognisable fodder or pieces; the clue appears corrupted in print
annotationWithheld.clue: £22 Eve collected for a decorative housing feature

clue.text: Walk round dim structure in London

indicators.note: round has the walking word wrapped around the word for dim

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
blear means dim or blurred

explanation.surface: Stroll around a gloomy London building.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a white marble triumphal arch at the west end of London's Oxford Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is a nineteenth-century triumphal arch, a landmark structure near Hyde Park in London.

clue.text: Compunction concerning Rome's destruction

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the letters of the city's name with its s are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: Rome plus the s of the possessive, all used as letters

explanation.surface: Guilt felt about the sacking of the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Compunction is a pang of guilt, and remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Beer round bar coming up for a large number

indicators.note: round puts the beer word around the reversed bar

parts.note: mild is a type of dark, lightly hopped beer

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the bar word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: Buying a round of beer at the bar for a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: MILD is a traditional British ale; 'round' looks like a round of drinks but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliard is a thousand million, the old British name for what is now called a billion.

clue.text: Blue-coated scholar from the Balkans ?

definitions.meaning: senior boys at Christ's Hospital, the Bluecoat School in Sussex, are known by this title
Greece lies in the Balkans, so something from there may be Greek

explanation.surface: A pupil in a blue coat who comes from south-east Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Christ's Hospital is an English school whose pupils wear long blue coats; its senior scholars were called Grecians.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the title of a senior Christ's Hospital pupil, and an adjective meaning of Greece, a Balkan country.

clue.text: NCO arranged dance-gets percentage for postponement

indicators.note: arranged puts the three letters of the soldier's abbreviation in a different order

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A non-commissioned officer organises a dance and takes a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: An NCO is a non-commissioned officer such as a sergeant; the term comes from the old London Stock Exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango was a fee paid on the Stock Exchange by a buyer to defer settlement to the next account.

clue.text: Seaweed twisted net and line

parts.note: tang is a large coarse seaweed, a kind of wrack

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of net are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Seaweed has got tangled in a fishing net and line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: What Tilden would do for a game?

definitions.text: What Tilden would do for a game?

parts.words: What Tilden would do for a game?
parts.note: Bill Tilden was a great American tennis champion, who would strike the ball before it bounced at the net

explanation.surface: Asking how a famous tennis player would win a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase describing Tilden's net play, hitting the ball in the air, also names a team sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played over a high net, its name describing striking a ball before it lands, as a tennis player does.

clue.text: Sprite said to be in Alaska

definitions.note: names a town located in Alaska, so a noun is meant

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the sprite's name, not its spelling

parts.note: a gnome is a sprite or goblin of folklore

explanation.surface: A rumour that a fairy lives in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent G of the folklore creature drops away when the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Nome is a gold-rush town on the coast of western Alaska.

clue.text: She could be Roman and head of the nursing staff

definitions.meaning: in ancient Rome a married woman of standing was given this title
the senior nurse in charge of a hospital

explanation.surface: A woman who might be from Rome and is in charge of the nurses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a respectable married woman of ancient Rome, and the senior nursing officer of a hospital.

clue.text: Considering printing material in article

indicators.note: in places the printing substance inside the word for article

parts.note: an article is a thing, an object
ink is what printing presses use

explanation.surface: Deliberating over what printing material is in some item.
explanation.definitionFit: Considering and pondering both mean turning something over in the mind.

clue.text: Particular centre of excitement?

indicators.note: centre of picks out the letters sitting at the middle of the word excitement

explanation.surface: A specific focus of thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a particular, a single detail or point in a list.

clue.text: Conduct of knight arranging rare Pole attempt

indicators.note: arranging the four letters of the word rare puts them in a new order

parts.note: N is the north pole
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A knight's behaviour in organising an unusual expedition to the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is the roving, adventurous conduct of a knight errant in search of chivalrous deeds.

clue.text: Laugh at the German team deprived of leader

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: the team word loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Mocking the German team after it lost its captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, to laugh scornfully at.

clue.text: Striking end of critical situation in court

definitions.meaning: the tip of a match, the end struck to light it
in tennis, on a court, the moment when one more point wins the whole contest

explanation.surface: The decisive conclusion of a tense moment during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court; 'striking' is lighting a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the head of a lucifer you strike, and the tennis moment when a single point decides the contest.
